title: Picking and moving a piece state diagram
description: How the player moves a piece on the 3D table, by clicking a piece and then a square, or by dragging it. A piece can be picked only when it belongs to the side in movable (set by the game screen; -1 when nobody may move) and that side is to move. Targets are the piece's legal moves from Chess.legal_moves. A press that picks nothing turns the camera instead (_orbiting), which is a separate concern left out here, as are the right button and the wheel. A move leaves the table as the move_made signal; the game screen decides what follows and shows the next position.

states.description: _selected = -1 and no drag: nothing lifted, no hints.
A piece is lifted, its square marked, gold dots on its quiet moves and rings on its captures.
The left button is down on the selected piece (_drag.moved = false).
The pointer has moved more than 6 pixels since the press (_drag.moved = true): the piece follows it above the board.
A pawn's move to the last rank was chosen: promotion_needed(from, to) was emitted and the piece stays selected while the game screen asks for the new piece.

transitions.guard: a piece of the movable side, which is to move

transitions.action: End the drag; the piece stays selected for a click on its target.

transitions.action: The piece follows the pointer, kept over the table.
